context: You are working at the welcome desk of a natural history museum. Listen to your manager and repeat what she says.
visual: A museum entrance hall with a ticket counter, a large whale model hanging from the ceiling and a cloakroom.
sentences: Tickets are sold here.
Students get a twenty percent discount.
Large bags must be left in the cloakroom.
The whale exhibition is on the ground floor to the left.
Guided tours for school groups need to be booked a week in advance.
The museum café on the first floor serves hot meals from noon until three o'clock.
If a visitor loses something, write down a description and their phone number, then pass the form to security.

context: You are helping out at the university's computer lab. Listen to the IT technician and repeat what he says.
visual: Rows of desktop computers, a large printer in the corner and a whiteboard with the Wi-Fi password.
sentences: Log in with your student ID.
Printing costs ten cents per page.
Save your files to the cloud, not the desktop.
All of the computers restart automatically every night at midnight.
If the printer jams, turn it off and wait a few seconds.
Students who forget their password can reset it through the university portal using their personal email.
Remind everyone that software installed on these machines is licensed only for academic use and cannot be copied.

context: You are training as a guide for the campus history walking tour. Listen to the tour leader and repeat what she says.
visual: An old stone building with a clock tower, surrounded by trees, with a group of students standing in front of it.
sentences: This is the old clock tower.
It was built over a century ago.
The original building was used as a library.
The clock was damaged by a storm in the nineteen fifties.
Today the tower houses the main offices of the university's history department.
Students traditionally gather here on graduation day to take photographs with their families.
From the top of the tower, which opens to visitors once a month, you can see the whole city.

context: You are volunteering at a wildlife rescue center. Listen to the veterinarian and repeat what he says.
visual: An animal care room with cages, a small owl wrapped in a towel and a vet checking its wing.
sentences: Wash your hands first.
Always wear gloves with the birds.
This owl was found with an injured wing.
Wild animals become stressed when people make loud noises.
Each animal's feeding schedule is posted on the door of its enclosure.
We try to limit human contact so that the animals don't lose their natural fear of people.
Once an animal has fully recovered, we release it as close as possible to the place where it was originally found.

context: You have just started working at the campus bookstore. Listen to the store supervisor and repeat what she says.
visual: A bookstore with shelves of textbooks, a rack of university sweatshirts and a cash register.
sentences: Textbooks are at the back.
We also sell used books.
Customers need a receipt to return an item.
Course books are organized by department and course number.
During the first week of term, the store stays open until eight p.m.
Students can sell their old textbooks back to us at the end of each semester for cash.
If a book is out of stock, offer to order it for the customer and explain that delivery usually takes five days.

context: You are training to work at a university astronomy observatory on public viewing nights. Listen to the astronomer and repeat what he says.
visual: A domed observatory at night with a large telescope pointing through an opening in the roof.
sentences: Let your eyes adjust slowly.
Please don't touch the telescope lens.
Tonight we will be looking at the planet Saturn.
Bright lights from phones make it harder to see faint stars.
The dome rotates so that the telescope can follow objects across the sky.
If the weather turns cloudy, we will move inside for a short presentation about the solar system.
Visitors are often surprised to learn that the light they see from some stars left them thousands of years ago.

context: You are starting a job at the university dining hall. Listen to the kitchen manager and repeat what she says.
visual: A busy cafeteria with a salad bar, hot food counters and students carrying trays.
sentences: Tie your hair back, please.
Lunch service starts at eleven thirty.
Every dish must show a list of allergens.
The salad bar needs to be refilled every twenty minutes.
Vegetarian and vegan options are kept on the separate green counter.
Food that has been out for more than two hours must be thrown away for safety reasons.
When students ask about ingredients and you aren't completely sure, check with the chef rather than guessing the answer.

context: You are training as a guide at a university's marine biology aquarium. Listen to the research coordinator and repeat what she says.
visual: A large aquarium tank with coral, small colourful fish and a sea turtle, with children pressing their hands to the glass.
sentences: Please don't tap the glass.
This turtle is fifteen years old.
Coral reefs are made by tiny living animals.
This tank recreates the water conditions of a tropical reef.
Our researchers study how rising ocean temperatures affect the growth of coral.
Visitors frequently ask whether the fish were caught in the wild, but all of them were bred here.
At the end of the tour, encourage guests to visit the touch pool, where they can gently handle starfish under supervision.
